questions.question: The correct definition of electrolysis is:
options: The chemical process in which electrical energy drives a non-spontaneous redox reaction
The spontaneous conversion of chemical energy into electrical energy
The splitting of molecules by heating them strongly
The movement of electrons through a salt bridge

questions.question: Which statement holds in EVERY electrochemical cell, galvanic or electrolytic?
options: The anode is the negative electrode
Reduction occurs at the cathode
The reaction is spontaneous
Electrons flow through the electrolyte

questions.question: The anode of an electrolytic cell is positive because:
options: Oxidation always creates positive charge
Electrons accumulate on it
Anions coat its surface
It is clamped to the positive terminal of the power supply, which pulls electrons out

questions.question: During electrolysis, the anions in the electrolyte migrate toward:
options: The cathode, where they are reduced
The power supply
The anode, where they are oxidised
Neither electrode — they stay in the middle

questions.question: An INERT electrode, such as the carbon rods used with copper chloride solution, is one that:
options: Dissolves slowly to feed the reaction
Conducts the current but contributes no atoms to the chemistry
Only works below room temperature
Blocks ions from reaching it

questions.question: The half-reaction at the ANODE during electrolysis of CuCl₂ solution is:
options: Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu
Cu → Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻
Cl₂ + 2e⁻ → 2Cl⁻
2Cl⁻ → Cl₂ + 2e⁻

questions.question: The observation at the cathode during electrolysis of CuCl₂ solution is:
options: A pink-brown layer of copper metal building up on the rod
Bubbles of gas with a sharp smell
The rod dissolving away
The solution turning a deeper blue

questions.question: The net reaction Cu²⁺ + 2Cl⁻ → Cu + Cl₂ is described as a DECOMPOSITION driven by electricity because:
options: The carbon electrodes break the compound apart mechanically
Heat from the current melts the salt
A stable compound is pulled apart into its elements, which would spontaneously recombine rather than separate
Chlorine decomposes the copper

questions.question: To plate a brass bangle with silver, the correct arrangement is:
options: Bangle as anode, silver bar as cathode, in any conducting solution
Bangle as cathode, silver bar as anode, in silver nitrate solution
Bangle and silver bar both as cathodes
Silver bar as cathode in copper sulfate solution

questions.question: During plating, the silver ion concentration in the bath stays constant because:
options: Silver ions are never actually removed
Extra silver nitrate is trickled in continuously
The current is too small to change it
The dissolving silver anode replaces every ion the cathode deposits

questions.question: The two standard reasons for electroplating an object are:
options: Corrosion protection and improved appearance
Increased magnetism and reduced mass
Higher melting point and flexibility
Electrical insulation and waterproofing

questions.question: In copper refining, impurities MORE reactive than copper, such as zinc and iron:
options: Fall to the floor of the tank as sludge
Plate onto the cathode along with the copper
Dissolve into the electrolyte and stay there, because the cathode reduces copper ions in preference
Never leave the impure slab

questions.question: The species that students most often forget to consider at the electrodes of an aqueous electrolysis is:
options: The sodium ion
Water itself, which can be oxidised or reduced
The chloride ion
The carbon of the electrodes

questions.question: Hydrogen, not sodium metal, forms at the cathode of a brine cell because:
options: Sodium ions are consumed at the anode instead
Hydrogen ions outnumber sodium ions
Sodium metal is denser than water
The sodium ion is extremely hard to reduce, so water accepts the electrons instead

questions.question: The sodium hydroxide produced in brine electrolysis appears:
options: As a coating on the anode
As a gas above the cathode
In the solution, where the remaining Na⁺ ions pair with the OH⁻ left when water is reduced
Only after the solution is boiled

questions.question: If the brine is allowed to become DILUTE, the anode product changes to:
options: Oxygen gas, because water then out-competes chloride at the anode
Sodium metal
Hydrogen gas
Nothing — the cell simply stops

questions.question: In the slope picture, an electrolytic cell corresponds to:
options: A ball rolling down the slope on its own
A motor hauling the ball back up the slope, paid for from the wall socket
A ball resting at the bottom forever
A turbine collecting energy from the roll

questions.question: A phone battery ON THE CHARGER is behaving as:
options: A galvanic cell
An open circuit
An electrolytic cell — the socket forces the discharge reaction to run in reverse
A resistor converting current to heat

questions.question: The fail-safe way to identify the anode in ANY cell diagram is to find the electrode where:
options: Electrons are being pulled off a substance — that is, where oxidation occurs
The plus sign is printed
The most bubbles appear
The wire is thickest

subtopics.title: A Silver Skin on a Steel Spoon

questions.question: In the electroplating chant, the object to be coated always hangs on:
options: The positive terminal
Either terminal, as convenient
The negative terminal, so the positive metal ions drift onto it and deposit
No terminal — it floats in the bath

questions.question: Calling the bar of plating metal 'the tin of paint and the refill service in one' means that it:
options: Dissolves to resupply the bath with ions at the same rate the object collects them
Stirs the bath as it rotates
Filters impurities out of the solution
Sets the colour of the coating

questions.question: Electroplating coats the hollow of a spoon's bowl evenly because:
options: The spoon is spun while it is coated
The coating arrives ion by ion wherever solution touches the surface, not stroke by stroke
Silver is sprayed on under high pressure
The hollow is heated more than the rest

questions.question: The sludge on a copper refinery's tank floor is valuable because it holds:
options: Concentrated copper sulfate crystals
Powdered carbon from the electrodes
Reactive metals like zinc and iron
Silver, gold and platinum that never dissolved at the cell's gentle voltage

subtopics.title: Salt Water In, Three Industries Out

questions.question: The single cheap input of the chlor-alkali process is:
options: Concentrated brine — salt water
Molten sodium metal
Hydrochloric acid
Sea sand

questions.question: Sodium ions 'queue and are refused' at the negative electrode because:
options: They are too large to touch the electrode
They are attracted to the positive electrode instead
Water is far easier to reduce, so the electrode serves water and makes hydrogen
Chlorine gas blocks their path

questions.question: The caustic soda left in the tank goes on to be used in:
options: Petrol refining and tyre manufacture
Soap-making and paper mills
Cement kilns
Glass blowing

questions.question: Which household trio all trace back to brine electrolysis?
options: Candles, matches and paraffin
Wool, cotton and leather
Bricks, tiles and cement
Pool chlorine, bleach and PVC piping
